# te-drift-detector

> Cross-turn scaffold/state drift detection for agent sessions. Catches gradual
> corruption of a conversation's working state that looks clean turn-by-turn but
> compounds into a compromised session. Zero required dependencies, deterministic
> by default, standard-library Python.

## What it does

Per-turn safety filters read each message in isolation and miss slow state
corruption: the running system scaffold / summary / context is nudged a little
each turn until the assumptions the model operates under have inverted, with no
single turn looking like an attack. te-drift-detector fingerprints each turn,
measures drift from a baseline and turn-to-turn velocity, and flags sustained
drift a per-turn check cannot see.

## Install

    pip install te-drift-detector

## CLI

    te-drift detect --attack-type poisoning      # analyze a built-in conversation
    te-drift detect --attack-type normal
    te-drift session --session-jsonl PATH        # analyze a session transcript (JSONL)
    te-drift session --session-jsonl PATH --mode sliding-window --window-size 10
    te-drift eval                                # run scaffold-corruption eval harness

## Python

    from te_drift import TEDriftDetector
    report = TEDriftDetector().run_conversation([(role, text), ...])
    report["threat_level"]        # NORMAL / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL
    report["anomalies_detected"]  # int

    from te_drift import load_turns, run_drift_analysis   # JSONL adapter
    from te_drift.evals import run_all                    # eval harness

## How it works

Eight per-turn features (facts, entities, sentiment, task framing, authority,
register, negations, vocabulary). Absolute drift vs. baseline plus velocity vs.
previous turn, combined with fixed weights. Anomaly if absolute drift > 0.50,
velocity > 0.30, 3+ component thresholds breached, or a known signature matches
(scaffold poisoning / persona drift / constraint bypass / scaffold interference).

Drift is lexical (set overlap) by default: deterministic and dependency-free.
Optional semantic embeddings via a local Ollama endpoint are opt-in with
TE_DRIFT_EMBED=1.

## Detect, then recover

te-drift-detector is the detect half of a pair. The recover half is hermes-blind
(https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind), a recovery scaffold injected
mid-conversation to pull a drifting session back toward baseline. Monitor drift
here; inject recovery with hermes-blind; confirm the trajectory bends back.

## Evidence and honest limits

The scaffold strongly shapes agent behavior (langquant recall A/B 0.83 vs. 0.00
across n=74 sessions, ~2.5x compression), which is why monitoring scaffold-state
integrity is worthwhile. It is strong influence on a small sample, not full
determination. Thresholds are conservative defaults; the feature set is
heuristic and English-oriented; meaning-preserving corruption can slip under
lexical drift. Complementary to per-turn filters, not a replacement.
